name: Stack
statusNote: Stack is a thin flexbox wrapper whose API (gap, direction, align, justify, wrap, padding, each optionally per viewport range) has been stable for several releases; alpha reflects Primer's caution, not unfinished behaviour.
summary: A one-dimensional layout primitive: children in a row or column with a gap from the stack spacing scale, cross-axis alignment, main-axis distribution, optional wrapping and padding, each settable per viewport range. Choose it for arranging siblings; choose page-layout for page regions.

inputs.name: gap
inputs.description: Space between children: 0, 4, 8, 12, 16 or 24px. Unset reads an inherited gap or else --stack-gap-normal (see notes). May be given per viewport range as {narrow, regular, wide}.

inputs.name: direction
inputs.description: Main axis: a column (vertical) or a row (horizontal). Responsive.

inputs.name: wrap
inputs.description: Whether children wrap onto further lines. Responsive.

inputs.name: padding
inputs.description: Padding on all four sides: 0, 4, 8, 12, 16 or 24px. Responsive.

inputs.name: paddingBlock
inputs.description: Top and bottom padding; overrides padding's block axis within the same viewport range. Responsive.

inputs.name: paddingInline
inputs.description: Start and end padding; overrides padding's inline axis within the same viewport range. Responsive.

inputs.name: children
inputs.description: The stacked items. Wrap one in a Stack.Item to let it grow or refuse to shrink.

inputs.name: itemGrow
inputs.description: Stack.Item grow: the item takes a share of the free main-axis space. Responsive.

inputs.name: itemShrink
inputs.description: Stack.Item shrink: false keeps the item at its content size when space runs out. Responsive.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.description: A flex box (column by default) with the gap between children and optional padding. It draws nothing: no fill, border or radius.

anatomy.name: Stack.Item
anatomy.description: An optional wrapper for one child that controls its grow and shrink; plain children behave like an Item with defaults.

variants.description: 4px between children, from the base scale.
12px between children, from the base scale.
16px between children; also the fallback when no gap is set anywhere above.
Children in a column, top to bottom.
Children in a row, start to end (mirrored in right-to-left).

layout.text: The container is a flex box: column by default, children stretched across the cross axis, wrapped lines packed at the start of the cross axis (align-content: flex-start).

The gap scale maps none 0, tight --base-size-4, condensed --stack-gap-condensed, cozy --base-size-12, normal --stack-gap-normal, spacious --stack-gap-spacious; the gap applies on both axes, so wrapped lines are separated by the same amount.

The padding scale maps none 0, tight --base-size-4, condensed --stack-padding-condensed, cozy --base-size-12, normal --stack-padding-normal, spacious --stack-padding-spacious, applied to all four sides.
paddingBlock and paddingInline use the same scale for one axis and win over padding for that axis within the same viewport range, because their rules follow padding's.
align maps start, center, end and baseline to the cross-axis alignment of the same name; stretch is the base rule and has no rule of its own.
justify maps start, center, end, space-between and space-evenly to main-axis distribution; there is no space-around.

An item's base is flex 0 1 auto with a minimum inline size of 0: it keeps its content size, may shrink below its content width, and never grows unless grow is set; shrink false fixes it at content size.

A responsive value is an object of narrow, regular and wide. The narrow value applies at every width (its rules sit outside any media query); the regular value overrides it from 768px (--viewportRange-regular, equal to --breakpoint-medium); the wide value overrides both from 1400px (--viewportRange-wide, equal to --breakpoint-xxlarge).
Stack.Item grow and shrink follow the same ranges: the narrow value at every width, regular from 768px, wide from 1400px.

behaviour.text: Stack has no interaction or motion; a range change re-lays the children instantly.

accessibility.role: none (generic container; the caller may render it as a list or another element)
keyboard: Not focusable; tab order is the children's source order, which a horizontal right-to-left layout or justify does not change.
semantics: Nothing is announced for the Stack itself.

notes.text: A Stack with no gap reads the --stack-gap custom property, which inherits: a nested Stack without its own gap takes its nearest ancestor Stack's gap instead of --stack-gap-normal. A native build should either reproduce this inheritance or document that unset means normal.
align stretch has no rule, so a responsive align such as {narrow: center, regular: stretch} stays centred at regular and wide: the narrow rule applies at every width and nothing resets it.

The narrow value is not limited to narrow viewports: {narrow: horizontal} alone makes the stack horizontal at every width. Resolve a responsive value as wide if set and width >= 1400, else regular if set and width >= 768, else narrow if set, else the base default.

A padding given for the regular or wide range overrides a paddingBlock or paddingInline given for narrow (or unranged), since later media-query rules win; within one range the axis-specific prop wins.

The viewport ranges are CSS media queries on the window width, written in rem (48rem, 87.5rem) and so scaled by the root font size; the JS twin hard-codes 768px and 1400px. A native build evaluates the window width each frame and should use the px values.

Layout is the browser's flexbox: free-space distribution, shrinking below content (min-inline-size 0), baseline alignment and wrapping with a two-axis gap. An immediate-mode build needs a two-pass measure (content sizes, then distribution) to match.
